claims.claim: An estimate counted in excess of 240,000 meteors during nine hours of the 1833 storm
claims.quote: another, done as the storm abated, estimated in excess of 240,000 meteors during the nine hours of the storm, over the entire region of North America east of the Rocky Mountains

claims.claim: One estimate of the peak rate was over 100,000 meteors an hour
claims.quote: One estimate of the peak rate is over one hundred thousand meteors an hour

claims.claim: The event was seen across North America east of the Rockies
claims.quote: over the entire region of North America east of the Rocky Mountains

claims.claim: The 1833 image is an Adolf Vollmy engraving after a painting by Karl Jauslin, public domain
claims.quote: The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin

claims.claim: In 1868 the Leonids reached about 1,000 meteors per hour in dark skies
claims.quote: Another strong appearance of the Leonids in 1868 reached an intensity of 1,000 meteors per hour in dark skies.

claims.claim: The Leonids enter the atmosphere at 70 km/s
claims.quote: the Leonids are fast moving streams which encounter the path of Earth and impact at 70 km/s (252,000 km/h; 156,590 mph)

claims.claim: The Leonids are the fastest annual meteor shower
claims.quote: It is the fastest annual meteor shower.

claims.claim: The second image is É. L. Trouvelot's 'The November Meteors', 1882, public domain
claims.quote: Archive title: File:Trouvelot - The November Meteors.jpg ... Date: 1882 ... Author: Étienne Léopold Trouvelot ... Licence: Public domain

claims.claim: The Trouvelot plate depicts meteors observed on the night of November 13–14, 1868
claims.quote: THE NOVEMBER METEORS. As observed between Midnight and 5 o'clock A.M. on the Night of November 13-14, 1868.

claims.claim: The meteor trails all appear to radiate back to a single point in the constellation Leo
claims.quote: The Leonids get their name from the location of their radiant in the constellation Leo: the meteors appear to radiate from that point in the sky.

claims.claim: The Tunis engraving was made from a sketch at the Casbah of Tunis, 27 November 1885
claims.quote: Étoiles filantes du 27 novembre 1885, D'après un croquis fait à la Casbah de Tunis, par M. Portanier.

claims.claim: The radiant point gave the shower its name
claims.quote: The name is derived from Greek and Latin with the prefix Leo- referring to the constellation and the suffix -ids signifying that the meteor shower is the offspring of, descendant of, the constellation Leo.

claims.claim: The Tunis sketch is public domain and credited to M. Portanier
claims.quote:
Author: M. Portanier
Licence: Public domain

claims.claim: The 1833 storm was caused by dust shed by the comet in 1800, not by its recent passage
claims.quote: The 1833 storm was not due to the recent passage of the comet, but from a direct impact with the previous 1800 dust trail.

claims.claim: The orbit diagram is from G. F. Chambers, The Story of the Comets, 1909
claims.quote:
Archive title: File:The story of the comets - Orbit of the leonids on nov. 13 and of the comet of 1866 (i.) relatively to the orbits of certain planets.jpg
Description: Orbit of the leonids on nov. 13 and of the comet of 1866 (i.) relatively to the orbits of certain planets
Date: 1909
Author: George Frederick Chambers

claims.claim: Comet Tempel–Tuttle is the source of the shower, identified in 1866
claims.quote: It was in 1866–67 that information on Comet Tempel-Tuttle was gathered, pointing it out as the source of the meteor shower and meteor storms.

claims.claim: Leonid storms return about every 33 years
claims.quote: The Leonids also produce meteor storms (very large outbursts) about every 33 years

claims.claim: It is still not understood whether a given trail will produce fireballs or fainter meteors
claims.quote: However, whether a specific meteoroid trail will be primarily composed of small or large particles, and thus the relative brightness of the meteors, was not understood.

claims.claim: The final photograph was taken by Alpsdake in Japan on 19 November 2001 and is public domain
claims.quote:
Description: Leonids  and  Orion  in Japan
Date: 2001-11-19
Author: Alpsdake
Licence: Public domain

claims.claim: The storm occurred on the night of 12–13 November 1833
claims.quote: it was the meteor storm of 12–13 November 1833 that broke into people's modern-day awareness

claims.claim: The Cheyenne established a peace treaty in connection with the event
claims.quote: the Cheyenne established a peace treaty and the Lakota calendar was reset

claims.claim: The Lakota calendar was reset and many Native American birthdays were later counted from that night
claims.quote: Many Native American birthdays were calculated by reference to the 1833 Leonid event.

claims.claim: Harriet Tubman and Frederick Douglass took note of the event
claims.quote: Abolitionists including Harriet Tubman and Frederick Douglass as well as slave-owners took note and others.

claims.claim: Abraham Lincoln commented on the event years later
claims.quote: Abraham Lincoln commented on it years later.

claims.claim: Joseph Smith called the event a literal fulfilment of the word of God
claims.quote: Joseph Smith, the founder and first leader of Mormonism, afterwards noted in his journal for November 1833 his belief that this event was "a litteral [sic] fulfillment of the word of God"

claims.claim: Denison Olmsted spent the last weeks of 1833 collecting reports
claims.quote: After spending the last weeks of 1833 collecting information, he presented his findings in January 1834 to the American Journal of Science and Arts

claims.claim: Olmsted found the meteors radiated from a point in Leo, that the shower was short, that Europe did not see it, and speculated the particles came from a cloud in space
claims.quote: He noted the shower was of short duration and was not seen in Europe, and that the meteors radiated from a point in the constellation of Leo and he speculated the meteors had originated from a cloud of particles in space.

claims.claim: In 1866–67 the parent comet was identified as Tempel–Tuttle
claims.quote: It was in 1866–67 that information on Comet Tempel-Tuttle was gathered, pointing it out as the source of the meteor shower and meteor storms.

claims.claim: A close encounter with Jupiter is expected to perturb the streams, making storms of historic size unlikely for many decades
claims.quote: However, a close encounter with Jupiter is expected to perturb the comet's path, and many streams, making storms of historic magnitude unlikely for many decades.
